answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (mandatory security patch), ruling out the b1 pattern. Read-replica routing (b5) addresses read load, but the symptom is write-path p99, so it is unlikely to help. Circuit breakers (b4) fit a failing dependency, which is not indicated. Add capacity (b3) is plausible given peak settlement traffic, but provisioning is slow and may not reverse a regression that began with the release. Regional failover (b2) is the memory-verified fast lever for latency recovery with clean traffic shift and no write loss; failing over to a healthy region can shed whatever degraded state the new build introduced while preserving all customer writes. Failover during peak writes carries replication-lag/write-loss risk, so that risk is flagged and the failover must be verified for write durability before committing traffic.
